To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure of the protein tyroxine kinase domain of c-Src kinase in complex with staurosoprine reveals structural differences in the ATP-binding site that may be relevant in understanding the catalytic mechanism.
the structure of C-terminal Src-kinase reveals a new mechanism for ATP-binding and a new molecular pivot for lobe movement.

we have determined the crystal structure of the catalytic domain of C-terminal src kinase (CSK), co-complexed to staurosporine and that the structure is most similar to the structures of other protein tyrosines kinases, c-Src, fibroblast growth-factor-receptor kinase 1 (FGFR1) and Hck, and least similar to the structure of insulin-receptor kinase (IRK).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural and functional characterization of protein kinases, in particular the Src kinase family, which are implicated in the regulation of cell division and cell growth.

the structural and biochemical characterisation of the C-terminal Src kinase, a member of the Src family of protein tyrosine and tyrosine kinase-related protein kinases, which are important in the regulation of cell signalling pathways.
understanding the structure of the catalytic domain of the protein tyrosl kinase, C-terminal Src kinase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the structure of the protein tyro-sine kinase domain of CSK in complex with stauros-po-rine is a very important structure for understanding the catalytic mechanism of protein tyrosine ki-nases.
this paper describes the first crystal structure of a protein tyrosine phosphatase.
the structure of the kinase of CSK in complex with staurosoprine is the first structure of a protein tyrosine-kinase in complex with an ATP-competitive inhibitor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the crystal structures of the protein tyroine kinase domain of CSK in complex with staurosoprine, and of CSK in the absence of ligand, have been determined to 2.4 and 2.5 A resolution, respectively.

the structure of the protein tyro-sine kinase domain of CSK in complex with stauros-porine reveals atomic details of inhibitor binding, and provides a framework for the design of novel, more selective inhibitors of protein tyrosine phosphorylation.
the structure of the protein tyro-sine kinase domain of c-terminal Src kinase (cSK) has been determined to a resolution of 2.4 Angstrom.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CSK is structurally distinct from other protein kinases, and that this may be due to the presence of an N-terminal lobe extension that is unique to CSK.

the structure of the kinase domains of CSK and c-Src are similar and that the binding mode of staurosporine in the CSK structure is very similar to the binding mode of the same inhibitor in the c-Src kinase structure.

CSK, which is a member of the Src family kinases (SFKs) and is the only one that is not constitutively active, is a good model to understand the mechanism of inhibition of SFKs by ATP-competitive inhibitors.
